milestones.title: Launch readiness items L1–L11
milestones.goal: Close every prerequisite before any public exposure: tagged links, share infra, AEO surface, error monitoring, submission path, correction link, freshness alarm, retention sensor, growth operator.
milestones.why: Each one protects a promise the product makes. L10 (correction link) and L11 (freshness alarm) came straight out of the pressure test as the two fatal risks to the word 'verified'.

milestones.title: Domain cutover — launch moment
milestones.goal: greenpoint.life serving, apex primary, AEO origin flipped, src tags surviving the redirect hop.
milestones.why: Launch was defined as the cutover, not a marketing event. Everything in the growth engine gates on it.

milestones.title: Rename to Stoopwise, stoopwise.com canonical
milestones.goal: Parent brand that survives the next neighborhood; greenpoint.life 308s here.
milestones.why: 'Greenpoint' left the brand, so every title and machine surface now has to carry it explicitly — that keyword is what search and answer engines match on.
milestones.consequence: The analytics host list had to be corrected on 8/6. stoopwise.com now carries 57% of all people ever recorded; the pre-correction rule would have dropped them.

milestones.title: Wave 1 supply gate passed
milestones.goal: ≥35 dated items upcoming in the next 7 days before spending the seeding.
milestones.why: Seeding a trust network is one-shot. An org note that says 'your events are live here' has to be true, and the feed has to reward the click.
milestones.outcome: 56 on 8/11 against a bar of 35. Held above the bar since 8/7. Highest ever recorded on every feed measure.

milestones.title: First outbound send — friends & family
milestones.goal: Break the deferred-send streak with the lowest-stakes group, on a tagged link.
milestones.why: Wave 1 had been deferred three times (8/6, 8/11, 8/12). The sneak-peek group is a real send with no cold-outreach risk, and it proves the attribution plumbing on a live audience.
milestones.outcome: Sent ~6:30pm over WhatsApp on ?src=friends-family. It landed: 15 people, 39 card opens, 4 high-intent actions — the first campaign link in the project's history to produce sessions, and proof the attribution plumbing works before the org notes go out.

milestones.title: Adversarial review of the seeding motion; P1–P6 ratified
milestones.goal: Two independent hostile passes over the wave before sending, then pre-register every rule pre-data.
milestones.why: Pre-registration is only legitimate before the data exists. Both passes converged on the same finding: the org notes are low-risk, Q2 is the fragile item.
milestones.outcome: Wave splits — org notes go now, Q2 moves to back-to-school. Six pre-registrations ratified. Two code items shipped same day.

milestones.title: Full-stack strategy review; P7–P11 ratified
milestones.goal: Two independent passes (adversarial + 2026 best-practices research) plus a category scan of the deck, the weekend before Wave 1.
milestones.why: The plan's rules all guarded against wrong readings; the likeliest fall failure was nothing starting — no signups, no R1, no submissions, no medium test. P7–P11 give that case dates, numbers, and agreed meanings, set while pre-data ratification was still legitimate.
milestones.outcome: P7–P11 ratified; Q2 dated Tue Sep 8; kids roster adds enter the 8/24 ingest; gtm-state became the primary send log with the shared? field. Send kit finalized in the roster. Both reviews endorsed the plan's shape.

milestones.title: Full-angle launch review; D1–D6 ratified
milestones.goal: Answer 'have we considered every angle' before spending the seeding — three independent passes plus a live ground-truth sweep of Greenpoint's attention infrastructure.
milestones.why: Batu asked for blindspots before poking a question and finding one. Passes: a first-principles design blind to our docs, an adversarial review judged only on speed-to-signal, and outside research on how hyperlocal products reached habit. All three converged: the plan acquired visitors and nothing retained them.
milestones.outcome: D1 re-registered the demand gate as a rate with a floor (pre-Wave-1-data, the last legitimate moment). D2–D6 approved as one act: weekly Monday send from 8/24, parallel reach with the 8/25 gate deleted, legal-only physical channel, five product return/measurement fixes, September supply pulled forward. Four factual claims verified in code first.

experiments.name: return_visit retention sensor
experiments.hypothesis: Not an experiment — the prerequisite. Without it there is no way to see whether anyone comes back, and the demand gate is unreadable.
experiments.smallestTest: localStorage first-seen + visit count. No fingerprinting, no accounts.
experiments.implication: Unlocks R1, R2 and the demand gate itself. The baseline is still young — nothing before 7/26 is recoverable.

experiments.name: Follow — personalized alert vs broadcast digest
experiments.hypothesis: Re-entry is the weakest edge of the content loop — nothing tells a resident it's a new week. A followed lens or place beats a broadcast digest at bringing them back.
experiments.smallestTest: Manual segments, 4–5 coarse ones. No backend, no automation build. Batu sends only when something matches.
experiments.rule: Segment click-through vs broadcast click-through over 3 weeks. Kill if segmented doesn't beat broadcast by week 3 → personalization isn't worth a backend, fall back to the digest and close the question. Time-boxed to 3 weeks either way.
experiments.actual: 5 signups (+1 on 9/4), 0 segmented. Control arm has now sent twice: 8/25 and 9/1. Across both sends 28 arrivals, 0 card opens, 0 events beyond pageview/return_visit, 27 of 28 out of region.
experiments.trigger: R1's COMPARISON still starts the first Monday after ≥10 signups with ≥1 segmented, 3-week clock from then (P5). D2 (2026-08-17) decoupled the digest itself: it sends weekly from Mon Aug 24 as the retention spine whether or not R1 arms. P7 fallback stands for the comparison.
experiments.implication: Trigger still unmet on both halves; R1's own 3-week clock untouched and should stay so. The broken tag recurred on the second send — 4 of 13 arrivals (31%) after 7 of 15 (47%) — because the 9/1 email was composed from the 8/25 one, which still carried the bad URL. The fix has to land in the sent email, not only in the readout draft. On two sends' evidence the count of clicks that produced a second in-product event is zero out of thirty, so D9's clicks-vs-list-size rule still cannot be read off it. The deeper constraint is list size: at five subscribers this channel cannot answer D9's question however well it is written.

experiments.name: Org seeding — 3 orgs already on the map
experiments.hypothesis: A recommendation from inside a small trust network converts where broadcast can't, and costs nothing. An org that shares is a Loop B ignition.
experiments.smallestTest: Three emails. Per-org src row added first.
experiments.rule: Sessions and activation rate per src. Kill an org-type after 2 non-responses.
experiments.target: ≥1 session per sent src within 7 days (P3 mechanism check)
experiments.actual: All 3 Wave-1 org srcs sent and now silent 18–22 days: Town Square 8/17 (1 person, last event 8/17), Library 8/18 (7 people, 3 card opens, 1 action, last 8/19), Brooklyn Craft 8/18 (8 people, 1 card open, last 8/21). No replies. Nothing has moved in seven days.
experiments.implication: Mechanism check still passes for all three. Kill rule still does not fire: institution 1, volunteer-org 1, business 1 counted, with Action City Comics excluded by cycle 7's ruling and Perri having replied. Q1 CLOSES AT THE SEP 15 READOUT by the four-week clock from the 8/17 first send, which makes cycle 8's two counting questions load-bearing for the first time — they have been open seven days and decide how Q1 closes. Town Square BK still has zero cards on the map, so preflight:send refuses that target and no follow-up should repeat 'your events are live here'. Q1's slot frees on 9/15, the first honest opening for R4 or per-lens .ics feeds.
experiments.notes: Org-type kill clock suspended for August (silence in vacation season is noise). Taxonomy: institution / business / volunteer-org. D3 (2026-08-17) supersedes P11's trigger: the arts wave no longer waits for Q1 to close — Film Noir sends this week alongside Wave 1, WORD and Flower Cat behind it. Sends consume no experiment slot.
experiments.source: growth §4; roster P4; strategy review P11; D3

experiments.name: Instagram carousel — the medium test
experiments.hypothesis: The neighborhood's attention lives on Instagram, not in browsers (Rana: 'people don't open browsers'). An auto-generated weekly carousel of the week's cards tests whether the CONTENT lands when the CONTAINER changes — the one open question that can invalidate the product's form rather than a feature.
experiments.smallestTest: Auto-generated from existing cards, 4 weeks, src=ig. No account grinding — that stays banned.
experiments.rule: In-feed engagement vs. tagged sessions. A carousel that engages while the site stays flat is evidence about the container, not the content.
experiments.implication: D3 moved this off P9's trigger ('Oct 6, only if tagged sessions are under 50'), which had scheduled our biggest open question as a consolation prize for failure — and would have suppressed it permanently on a merely-mediocre result. Its answer is worth most while it can still shape September.
experiments.caveat: A carousel measures in-feed engagement, not whether anyone would return to anything. Pair its read with the digest's open-vs-click, which is the cleaner medium instrument.
experiments.source: strategy review D3; growth 'Explicitly not doing'; learning-log Q1
experiments.notes: D9 (2026-08-19) pre-registered how this instrument reads alongside the digest: its in-feed-engagement-vs-tagged-sessions rule now feeds the container trigger, and its result can close learning-log Q1 either way. See rules.medium-pivot-preregistered.

experiments.name: AEO / answer-engine acceptance
experiments.hypothesis: Cards published as static structured HTML get cited by search engines and AI assistants, bringing residents at zero cost to acquire.
experiments.smallestTest: Already shipped. Watch organic sessions monthly.
experiments.actual: ChatGPT 16 people over six days (8/29–9/7), 9 of 16 opening a card, 22 opens. Search: 20 clicks and 425 impressions in the 8/30–9/5 window against 8 and 248 the week before, average position 13.7 -> 10.5. Google 45 people, 91% local.
experiments.implication: Fifth positive read, and the first that survives its own caveat — the assistant traffic is no longer one day. Against that, the first live Search Console read says ZERO generic-intent queries: all 13 are place-name or event lookups, so Google is not sending us 'what's happening in Greenpoint' traffic, it is sending people who already have a name in their head. Loop C is working, but through the corpus rather than through the question the loop was drawn around. Recorded, not graduated; no kill rule by design.
experiments.notes: Crawl latency measured at ~4 days — survivable for a card dated a week out, fatal for one posted the morning of. That is an ingest lead-time fact. P10 (2026-08-15): citations and AI-referrer sessions get their own readout lines — citations up with sessions flat is the loop working zero-click, never a fail read; llms.txt booked at zero.
experiments.source: growth §4; readout Finding 2; strategy review P10

experiments.name: Funnel read
experiments.hypothesis: Where do first sessions stall — before the first card open, or between open and act?
experiments.smallestTest: Analysis only, inside the readouts. No build until this is read.
experiments.actual: 329 people -> 58 opened a card (18%) -> 25 acted. Locals 139 -> 41 (29%) -> 12 activated (9%).
experiments.implication: Eighth reading at growing n, all eight agree: the stall is before the first card open. Locals have now held at 29% card-open conversion for three consecutive cycles while the population grew by 54, which makes it a property of the product rather than of a cohort. The two populations that do not stall there are assistant arrivals (9 of 16) and search arrivals.

experiments.name: Opinionated default on first visit
experiments.hypothesis: Landing new visitors in the merchandised 'this week' state fixes whatever A1 says the stall point is.
experiments.rule: First-session activation rate. Kill if flat after 2 weeks.
experiments.implication: Waits for a free slot. All three are spoken for the moment Wave 1 fires.

experiments.name: Post-value prompt timing
experiments.hypothesis: The email ask fires too late (or too early) relative to demonstrated value.
experiments.rule: Signup rate per activated session, pre/post.
experiments.implication: Deferred until ≥50 sessions/week. Below that it's noise.

experiments.name: 'New this week' marker
experiments.hypothesis: Badging cards added since a reader's last visit makes the weekly rhythm visible in-product.
experiments.smallestTest: Small UI change over existing first-seen data.
experiments.rule: Return-visit card_open depth pre/post. Kill if no lift after 2 weeks of returners.
experiments.implication: Needs a returner population to exist first. Today's WRL proxy is 2 people.

experiments.name: Five warm-user conversations
experiments.hypothesis: What would make you check this weekly? And the causal question: did Stoopwise cause you to do something you wouldn't otherwise have known about or chosen?
experiments.smallestTest: Five conversations. Small-n qualitative is a valid instrument at this scale.
experiments.rule: Qualitative. Feeds Tuesday proposals and the pilot kit.
experiments.implication: The causal question is the demand-side twin of the unique-coverage count, and verbatim the strongest line pilot evidence can carry.

experiments.name: Anonymous save / star
experiments.hypothesis: Saving starts the resident participation graph and returns readers to their own shortlist. Laura and Edmond's standing ask.
experiments.smallestTest: Small UI change over localStorage. No backend, no identity.
experiments.rule: Proposed: save rate per activated session, and whether savers return more. Kill if saves stay rare after 3 weeks or don't correlate with return. Final kill criteria set at launch of the experiment.
experiments.implication: Enters via a Tuesday proposal when a max-3 slot opens; Batu ratifies.

gates.name: Demand
gates.bar: PMF gate (re-registered 2026-08-17, D1): of locals who visit twice, ≥25% return in ≥3 of any 4 consecutive weeks, floor 12 people. risks.title: Safari deletes the retention sensor's storage at exactly our cadence
risks.severity: accepted and measured — one-directional, can only depress the gate
risks.detail: returnVisit.js is localStorage-only. Safari (ITP) clears script-written storage after ~7 days of browser use without a first-party visit — a weekly-check product sits precisely on that edge, so an iPhone user returning on day 8 can re-register as brand new with weekIndex 0, forever. Verified as unenumerated: no ITP or eviction row exists in environmental-dependencies.md. Consistent with our own data — the July round saw 7 of 24 return inside a 5-day window, while cross-week WRL shows 2.
risks.response: RULED 2026-08-19 (Batu): the server-set cookie mirror is DROPPED, not deferred — privacy.html promises no cookies in three places and the bias only runs one way (an evicted reader re-registers as new, inflating the denominator and deflating the numerator, so it can produce a false fail but never a false pass). Replaced by a return-rate-by-browser-family line in the Tuesday readout plus a labeled October read. Home-screen install still exempts a user; a tagged digest click counts as a return under D1 regardless of storage. DECISION_LOG 2026-08-19 sixth entry.

risks.detail: Sends ~2h, group answers ~3h, physical ~4–5h, the weekly send ~1h, conversations ~2h. Every researched hyperlocal success ran on years of unpaid founder labor, and the most repeated failure was exhaustion before the curve turned.

rules.text: Max 3 live experiments. Attribution dies past that.
Every experiment ships with hypothesis → smallest test → one metric → decision rule → kill criteria written before launch. No kill criteria, no launch.
Pre/post and small-n qualitative only. No A/B infrastructure, no significance theater — at this traffic it's noise cosplay.
September reads carry the autumn-rebound confound and nothing graduates on a Sep–Oct read alone. Carve-out: contemporaneous-control designs (R1, Q2) are exempt — 2a governs pre/post reads.
Each Q experiment closes at the readout after its rule fires, or after 4 weeks, whichever comes first. No experiment squats on a slot.
The unit of seeding is a small trust network, not reach. Saturate one network before opening the next.
Batu sends every outbound message. Every link is copied from channel-links.md, never composed by hand.
Paid acquisition is dead permanently, not deferred — revenue per user is $0, so only near-zero-CAC channels can ever fit.
Coverage is never for sale. Every verified business is on the map free.

P7: if R1 hasn't armed by the Mon Oct 5 readout, the next free slot goes to a no-list re-entry mechanism (R4 or per-lens .ics), and the late-Oct demand read is labeled 'measured without a re-entry mechanism' — a miss under it is never read as product failure alone.

P8: a demand-gate pass on cohorts wholly inside Sep–Oct is provisional until a Nov-or-later cohort clears the same bar — or it's accepted explicitly as a peak-season pass and disclosed in pilot conversations. Counterpart to the Dec–Feb no-read rule.

D3 (2026-08-17) supersedes P9's trigger: the IG carousel starts NOW, not 'Oct 6 if under 50 sessions'. P9 had scheduled the only test of the medium question as a consolation prize for failure, on a trigger a mediocre result would have suppressed permanently.

D4: physical means hand-to-hand at markets, permission-based placement inside venues, The Greenline, and being present at events. NEVER poles, parks, or scaffolding — §10-119 makes each flyer a separate $75–150 offence with the name on it presumed liable; 56 RCNY §1-05(c) requires a permit in parks.

P10: citations and AI-referrer sessions get their own readout lines. Citations up with sessions flat = Loop C working zero-click — H5's fail branch can't fire on it. llms.txt stays up, zero value booked.

P11's ORDER stands (Film Noir → WORD → Flower Cat) but D3 dropped its trigger and its 'never two networks at once' clause: the arts wave sends this week alongside Wave 1. Echo-chamber doctrine is about density INSIDE a network; per-src tagging already separates unrelated ones. Founder hours still point at parents.

The approved slate costs ~12–15 founder-hours/week through mid-September, and Batu confirmed that budget is realistic (2026-08-19) — so the slate runs as approved. The researched failure pattern most likely to end this is solo-operator exhaustion, and its earliest sign is a skipped week. Cut order, held in reserve if the real budget drops to 8 hours: fewer group-answer posts, one market morning instead of two, Greenline deferred.

rules.text: D9 (ratified 2026-08-19, pre-data): the medium test is judged on tagged clicks, never opens. Three consecutive sends with ?src=digest clicks <10% of list size, carousel engaging while src=ig sessions stay flat, OPENS the container ruling (email-first vs status quo) — it never executes a pivot. Container evidence never resets the demand clock (D1 counts tagged email clicks as returns). Three sends with clicks ≥25% of list closes learning-log Q1 in the site's favor and retires 'wrong container' as an explanation for a demand miss.

D7 (ratified 2026-08-19): Batu clears the queue once a day in a ~15-minute window — sends to approve-and-paste, branches to merge, rulings due. The queue is this file's `daily` + `needBy` fields, rendered in the cockpit; the operator keeps it current across sessions and chases items rather than waiting to be asked. The Tuesday readout reports the age of the oldest open queue item, target under 1 day. Supervision is unchanged — same approvals, daily clock.

D8 (ratified 2026-08-19): a build item that is already ratified in the DECISION_LOG, has NO visual surface, and carries test coverage merges by default 24h after its preview lands in the daily queue unless vetoed. Initial class, now: FB webview instrumentation and GSC plumbing (the routine-clobber fix already landed 2026-08-19; the gl_first_seen cookie mirror was DROPPED the same day — it would have falsified privacy.html's 'no cookies' promise, which is exactly the boundary this class draws). Anything visual keeps preview review (2026-08-08 design-batch rule). Named exception to growth-engine §7's 'code merges stay human'; one-strike demotion applies. Venue/category pages ratified in the same ruling as owned Loop C infrastructure — outside the max-3 cap, no kill rule, normal preview review, sequenced after the measurement repairs and the signup-ask redesign.

Standing rule (2026-08-19): a published promise is a constraint on the build, not a document that follows it. Anything that would falsify a live legal or trust page (privacy.html, terms, coverage standards) leaves any auto-merge class and becomes a decision for Batu, whatever its prior ratification. Set by the dropped cookie mirror, which was ratified twice and still stopped.

Scope is every parents-facing action, not just Q2.
